body.text: The 2026 ARIA Awards celebrated the very best in Australian music at the Hordern Pavilion in Sydney, with Perth's Tame Impala/Kevin Parker coming out on top.
Look at how the night unfolded on our blog.

So long, farewell, auf wiedersehen, goodnight
It's been a good night, especially for Tame Impala/Kevin Parker, but alas, all good things come to an end, and we must bid you adieu.
Check out all the highlights from tonight's awards below.
And here's the full list of winners:
A subdued ARIAs, but one that ripped along
As always, ARIA night has been a whirlwind. They really just whipped right through all the awards.

It was a fairly uncontroversial night; as expected people came out against AI (although we didn't think Sir Elton John would be among them!). It reflects ARIAs priorities too. It explicitly banned AI-generated music from the charts back in August.
Some final thoughts from me:
• Loved G Flip urging everyone to go out and support live music.
• Love love loved her drummer Benji Ellingworth telling everyone to respect their crew on tour, the unsung heroes of Australian music.
• And Fanny Lumsden shouting out Dolly Parton.
• And Miss Kannina talking about how important immigrants are to Australian society.
• But I reckon Genesis Owusu was robbed. No wins from eight nominations? When his record is one of the best of the year in my humble opinion? Devastating, for me, personally.
• Still, I'm happy for Kevin Parker/Tame Impala for all his wins. But I encourage any late-stage fans to go back to his 2008 self-titled EP. It's still an all-timer for me.

• And I hope you, like me, use the ARIA Awards to discover some new music you might not have gotten around on your own. For me, it was BOY SODA, because honestly I tend to just listen to the songs I loved as a teenager.
• There's just so much good Australian music!!
Key Event
We're all winners at the ARIAs
Another ARIAs done and dusted.
Tim and Mel were great hosts, the performances were all fantastic, and a bit of fiery talk about AI kept the passion up throughout.

It's a great list of winners this year too, Tame Impala and Ecca Vandal deserve all the plaudits. My thoughts to Genesis Owusu, who does not deserve to leave empty handed, but he does have a few trophies at home so we're confident he'll be OK.
Whether your favourite artist had a win tonight or you've never heard of any of these acts, please don't stop listening to Australian music.
Our scene is extraordinarily strong, and we need to continue to support it to keep it that way.
Buy a ticket, a T-shirt or a record from an emerging Australian act tomorrow and help them keep the fire burning.
Spiderbait gives roaring final performance of the night
The newly minted ARIA Hall of Famers are singing a medley of fan favourites: Calypso, Buy Me a Pony and Black Betty.

It's fun to see the band of Whitt, Kram and Janet English rock out as if they're not all in their 50s, drummer Kram wearing a no-AI T-shirt, bassist English in a sequinned dress, and guitarist Whitt in a leather jacket.
I love these songs and I love to see a band that's still their original line-up, 35 years after they first got together as teenagers living in regional NSW.
Kram even dedicated Black Betty to "Kev" aka tonight's big winner, Kevin Parker/Tame Impala.
Here's hoping for a Grand Slam 30-year anniversary tour in 2029, after they did one for Ivy and the Big Apples earlier this year. I'll see you there.
Key Event
Tame Impala knows you struggle with change
After acknowledging the Tame Impala Is Just One Guy meme in his past speech, Kevin Parker takes a moment during his Album of the Year speech to acknowledge how his ever-changing sound is met by fans.
Every album I’ve made has ruffled the feathers of fans and that’s kind of by design.
It didn't ruffle too many feathers though.
This win takes Parker to seven wins for the night, a grand total of 22 career awards, more than anyone else!
I told you so: It's Tame Impala's year!
Now he's copped Album of the Year, as predicted, Perth's own Tame Impala/Kevin Parker has won a whoppin' seven ARIAs tonight, including the Global Impact Award.

He was leading the nominations, with eight, and only lost two categories, Best Alternative Release and Best Dance/Electronic Release (I know, the numbers seem weird, but Global Impact wasn't in the nominations).
That puts him at 22 total ARIA wins since the release of his first album, Innerspeaker, in 2010. He's just beaten John Farnham and Silverchair to become the artist with the most ARIA awards ever.
Tame Impala wins Album of the Year
• BOY SODA — Soulstar [Warner Music Australia]
• DMA'S — DMA'S [Wonderlick Recording Company / Sony Music]
• Tame Impala — Deadbeat [Columbia Records / Sony Music]
Funny for Tame Impala to land Best Solo Artist after winning Best Group at past ARIAs
We know as well as anyone that Tame Impala is and always was a one-man band (at least as a recording artist).
But because the act presented as a band, especially on stage, until relatively recently... well, Tame Impala has picked up three, yes, three, ARIAs for Best Group: in 2013, 2015 and 2020.
Only now, does it make sense for Parker to take all the glory and win Best Solo Artist.
Still, it's no weirder than him being up for seemingly every genre, from pop to alternative to dance/electronic.
(Brush up on everything Kevin Parker with this history of his seminal album Currents.)
Tame Impala wins Song of the Year
• FISHER — Blackberries [etcetc Music Pty Ltd]
• G Flip — Bed on Fire [AWAL Recordings]
• Keli Holiday — Dancing2 [GROUP SPEED]
• Lithe — Cannonball [10K / ADA]
• Royel Otis — car [Ourness / Capitol Records]
• Sonny Fodera — Think About Us [Solotoko / ADA]
• Tame Impala — Dracula [Columbia Records / Sony Music]
• Vance Joy — Divine Feelings [Mushroom Music]
Tame Impala's Dracula does not suck
Song of the Year is another publicly voted award and you cannot fault the taste of the masses: Tame Impala's Dracula is an absolute banger.

It was the first Tame Impala song to chart on the US Billboard Hot 100, came third in the most recent triple j Hottest 100, and its remix featuring K-Pop icon Jennie took the song to a whole new stratosphere earlier this year.
"Hi, me again," Parker says when accepting the award.
Is his night over? Or does he have space for more pointy trophies?
Tame Impala wins Best Solo Artist
• BOY SODA — Soulstar [Warner Music Australia]
• G Flip — Dream Ride [AWAL Recordings]
• Ninajirachi — WannaCry [NLV RECORDS]
• Troye Sivan — She's The Best [EMI Music Australia]
Karnivool bag the win
Perth's Karnivool win the Best Hard Rock/Heavy Metal Album for the second time, after picking up the same award way back in 2013.
Fans were hanging out a long time for this record, and it was clearly worth the wait.
It's also one of the heaviest Australian albums to feature bagpipes in quite some time.
Karnivool wins Best Hard Rock/Heavy Metal Album
• Cosmic Psychos — I Really Like Beer [G.Y.R.O.]
• Karnivool — In Verses [Cymatic Records / Sony Music]
• WAAX — Angel's Mess [AWAL/DRUNK ON POWER RECORDS]
DMA'S win Best Rock Album
• Teen Jesus and the Jean Teasers — Glory [Community Music]
• The Belair Lip Bombs — Again [Third Man Records / Rocket]
• The Temper Trap — Sungazer [Mushroom Music]
Ecca Vandal wins Best Independent Release
• 2charm — boyfriend [STAR SCUM RECORDS]
• Ninajirachi, Porter Robinson — WannaCry [NLV RECORDS]
Sir Elton pops up to slam AI
Sir Elton John was the first ever host of the ARIA Awards back in 1987.
In its 40th year, he appears again, this time via video and to send a message to the Australian governement.
You have a duty to protect Australian artists and their work. Don't let AI use any artists' work without full permission.
Loading
Key Event
Tama Impala wins Global Impact Award
Presenting Tame Impala with the Global Impact Award, Darren Hayes compared him to Prince, David Bowie and the Beatles. Big praise!
He also called him "magically earnest and effortlessly cool", with the "production talent of Brian Eno", and spoke about how he'd inspired him as an artist.
The Global Impact Award is for an artist who has been influential and/or successful overseas over the past year.
It's only the second year the prize has been awarded, with Dom Dolla taking out the inaugural award last year.
It's just one award for Kevin Parker, who was up for another eight awards tonight, and has already won awards for best pop release, producing and engineering so far.
It's been a huge year for him so far, with his single Dracula spending 18 weeks in the top 10 of the ARIA Singles chart, as he headed on a 91-date global tour.
Key Event
Miss Kaninna gives it up for hip hop
Even if you don't consider yourself a hip hop fan, you should hear Miss Kaninna's excellent mixtape Blackprint.
She melds a broad variety of genres that have inspired her over the years and the whole record pulses with a punk energy. It goes beyond one genre.
But in her speech, she recognises the power of hip hop, especially in Australia.

Hip hop is so important to me because it gives me an opportunity to talk about how I feel about my Blak experience in this f***ing country, and it also makes me realise that there are so many other people in this country whose voices need to be heard.This country would be nothing without immigrants, and who you vote for in the next coming election is really f***ing important.

Hip hop is so important to me because it gives me an opportunity to talk about how I feel about my Blak experience in this f***ing country, and it also makes me realise that there are so many other people in this country whose voices need to be heard.
This country would be nothing without immigrants, and who you vote for in the next coming election is really f***ing important.
Miss Kaninna wins Best Hip Hop/Rap Release
• Nerve — Growing Pains [Nerve MP3's / Xelon Digital]
Matt Corby is all grown up
Best Adult Contemporary Album has been won by all the greats – Paul Kelly, John Farnham, Crowded House, Missy Higgins and more.
Matt Corby is the latest addition to this esteemed list, thanks to his Tragic Magic album from earlier this year. It was his first nomination in the category.
Corby wasn't there to accept, but he did recently chat with Al Newstead about not just this record but his career thus far. His is easily one of the best Australian Idol success stories.
Matt Corby wins Best Adult Contemporary Album
• Paul Kelly — Seventy [EMI Music Australia]
• Vika & Linda — Where Do You Come From? [Mushroom Music]
• Way Dynamic — Massive Shoe [Spoilsport Records]
The most A-list celebs?
Who are the most A-List celebrities present?- E
Who are the most A-List celebrities present?
- E

I don't feel comfortable calling people A-list or not, but I will name some celebrities in the crowd: Mel C from the Spice Girls, Abbie Chatfield and Keli Holiday, G Flip, and Tame Impala/Kevin Parker.
Key Event
Kevin Parker: king of pop
I’ve generally been pretty confident about Tame Impala’s chances tonight, but I thought the Best Pop Release award would be the hardest for Kevin Parker to take home.

Not because he isn’t deserving – he’s made some of the best pop songs in recent memory – but he was up against G Flip, Troye Sivan, newcomers Blusher and the woman who has won this award more times than anyone, Kylie Minogue.
This is the first time that Parker has won Best Pop Release, which he won for his brilliant earworm Dracula, written with fellow Aussie Sarah Aarons.
I feel like it's had a life of its own. I feel like I've just been sitting back and watching it grow into the superstar that it is. I'm so proud of the song and the life that it's had.
Tame Impala wins Best Pop Release
• Blusher — Rager [Warner Music Australia]
• G Flip — Dream Ride [AWAL Recordings]
• Kylie Minogue — Tension Tour//Live 2025 [Mushroom Music]
Key Event
Tim Minchin 'does words' on AI
Introducing the award for best original soundtrack or musical theatre cast album, Tim Minchin took on AI.
Art is not just content, it's content plus intent.
Art is an offer made by a human struggling to reflect the experience of being human for the sake of other humans.
At the heart of what makes our art singular, unique are our limitations,
Because our work, the music we make, is not just the result of our influences. It's born of what we've not listened to.
It isn't just the sum total of our excellence and craft. It's just as much a result of our flaws.
As much as anything, our music is a reflection of our imperfections, our self-doubt and self-loathing.
It's the endless hours, it's our shitty, f*****-up, striving, stumbling, needy, petty, hopeful, heartfelt, f***ing human-ness.
Art is the way we reach out to one another and it is defined and made beautiful by the glorious messiness of its human creators.
This will only remain true if we assert it as true and act accordingly
Which is to say: AI can suck my balls.
My Brilliant Career wins Best Original Soundtrack or Musical Theatre Cast Album
• Amanda Brown — Deadloch Season 1 [Amazon Content Services under exclusive licence to Strange Loops Recordings]
• Francois Tetaz — My Brilliant Career [Netflix]
Getting to know didgeridoo virtuoso and composer William Barton
If you don't already know William Barton from his extraordinary work as a didgeridoo virtuoso and composer, you might recognise him from sharing the stage with Kylie Minogue at the AFL Grand Final.

The ABC Classic recording, Gift — Our Breath of Life, is the world premiere recording by Omega Ensemble of Barton's music composed for Sydney Dance Company's Continuum, choreographed by Stephen Page in 2025.
Barton has described the music as a dedication "to the memory of one’s breath, the first breath we take as we are born into this world, and the last taken". This is Barton's third ARIA win.
William Barton wins Best Classical Album
Ecca Vandal wins Best Cover Art
• Connor Dewhurst for Amy Shark — soft pop [Wonderlick Recording Company / Sony Music]
Confirmed: BTS are popular
Most Popular International Artist is one of the few publicly voted awards, and has always been dominated by seriously big name acts.
They don't come much bigger than BTS and the Army that surrounds them. So not a huge surprise to see them take out the award this year.
"Sadly BTS couldn't be here to accept the award," host Tim McDonald quipped after announcing the winner.
BTS wins Most Popular International Artist
• BTS — ARIRANG [Virgin Music Group / Geffen]
• Olivia Rodrigo — you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love [Geffen / Universal Music Australia]
Key Event
Our first AI reference?
Laneway Festival won the award for Best Festival for the second year running, following a hugely successful run early this year headlined by Chappell Roan.
Founder Danny Rogers wasn't much in the mood for celebrating, dedicating his speech to "original music" in protest against AI.
Original music and live music simply don’t exist without incredibly talented and dedicated human beings.

At a time when their livelihoods are increasingly under threat, I want something to be really clear; Laneway stand firmly behind ARIA, PPCA and all artists fighting to protect the copy rights and creative rights.
There has never been a more important time to make noise about this.
The misuse of AI poses a real threat to our industry and things could change much faster than anyone realises.
We simply cannot take human creativity for granted, we need to protect the people who make the music we all love.
Is Tame Impala at the ARIAs?
Is Tame Impala present in person?- E
Is Tame Impala present in person?
- E
He sure is. And it's not unprecedented. He was last there in 2015, when Currents won Album of the Year.
And it's not like he skipped the 2020 event on purpose, when he won the same award for The Slow Rush.
It's just that it was a COVID-safe event!
Donny Benét wins Best Jazz Album
• Donny Benét — Il Basso [Donnyland Records / The Orchard]
• Hilary Geddes — Redleaf [Earshift Music]
• The Vampires — Skydancer [Earshift / The Planet Company]
Reports from the room!
I've used my charm to get the incredibly funny, famous and fantastic Jordan Barr and Luka Muller from triple j to give us a vibe check from inside the room:
3% and Scribe put on on an UNREAL performance of Not Many (Ganay Biralunbar) with live yidaki, like a dozen dancers and some PYROTECHNICS.
The general vibe is everyone is here to finally switch off for a night and reflect on all their hard work.

The music industry is a brutal, non-stop treadmill designed to always look to the next single, the next album, the next tour - so it doesn’t matter who “wins”, all these incredible Aussie artists are SO deserving of a night to look back on and celebrate the literal blood sweat and tears that goes into every line of every song.
Here's some evidence that they are actually there. Don't they look great?
The new king of jazz?
As always, the nominees for Best Jazz award were all awesome. We have so much talent in this country.
But I am personally stoked that the magnificent Donny Benét has won Best Jazz Album for his Il Basso record.
Donny is one of the great musicians in the country and a man who never takes himself too seriously. He’s a must-follow on Instagram and his music videos are stunning.
This is his first ARIA Award, though I’d hazard a guess that he has played on a few ARIA award winning albums in his time as a backing musician.
Congrats from the whole team here at the ABC News online ARIAs 2026 live blog, Donny.
Here’s some gushing from many years ago if you want to know more.
Key Event
A full orchestral glow-up for Bluey

Australia's beloved Blue Heeler family have done it again, with their third ARIA win for Best Children's Album. Bluey: Up Here gives music from favourite Bluey episodes like Sleepytime and Ice Cream a full orchestral glow-up.
It was recorded in Bluey's hometown, Brisbane, with more than 100 mostly local musicians, including the Queensland Symphony Orchestra and Camerata.
Music has always been a huge part of the show. Many credit lead composer Joff Bush and the Bluey music team with inspiring a whole new generation of classical music fans.
Bush says it's not something they set out to do, but it is something he's proud of.
“I don’t think kids often get the opportunity to find a connection with pieces of classical music,” he told ABC Classic in April.
Bluey wins Best Children's Album
• Emma Memma — Jungle Picnic [G.Y.R.O.]
• Play School — Dance It Out [ABC Music / The Orchard]
Amyl can't stop winning
Amyl & the Sniffers were the big winners at last year's ARIAs.
They're up for fewer awards this year, but have still managed to go home with some silverware thanks to their appearance in a car ad!
I'll be honest, I'm not sure who those people were who accepted this award. But here's a quote:
"Thank you to everyone involved"
Laneway Festival wins Best Music Festival
• Beyond The Valley 2025 — Untitled Group
• CMC Rocks — CMC Rocks Pty Ltd
• Groovin The Moo Lismore — Fuzzy Operations Pty Ltd
• Laneway Festival — ST JEROME'S LANEWAY PTY LTD
• Spilt Milk — Kicks Entertainment
Amyl and the Sniffers wins Best Use of an Australian Recording in an Advertisement
• Uber Eats: The Man LAROI — Special, The Kid LAROI
Engineering dropout loves to engineer
It’s quite funny that engineering dropout Kevin Parker has won an award called Best Engineered Release for the sixth time.
Turns out he just wasn’t studying the right kind of engineering.
Sound is my passion, it’s the thing I’m obsessed over most when making an album.
Not Drowning, Waving wins Best World Music Album
• Not Drowning, Waving — Malira [ORiGiN Recordings / ADA]
• The Cat Empire — Live At Sydney Opera House [BMG]
Tame Impala wins Engineer — Best Engineered Release
G Flip wins Best Video
• Stampede — Genesis Owusu, Isaac Brown [Ourness / Believe]
• Bed On Fire — G Flip, Tas Wilson [AWAL Recordings]
Was that the best performance of the night?
I would not want to go on stage after that absolute masterclass from 3%, Scribe and Fred Leone.
Their take on Scribe's anthemic 2003 single Not Many was Fox Sports's soundtrack for the NRL finals, which has earned it a nomination for Best Use of an Australian Recording in an Advertisement.
It's so great to see such a great song get a new life.
Key Event
DMA'S didn't think they'd win, but they're happy to be there
One of tonight’s favourites to take out multiple awards, rock trio DMA’s graced the red carpet, sunnies on.
The group just won Best Group and was nominated for Album of the Year, Best Rock Album and Best Video, but told ABC News on the red carpet the awards were not front of mind.
“We’re never confident like that, we’re just happy to be here,” guitarist Johnny Took said.
All three agreed the real thrill of attending the evening is supporting Australian-made music.
“It's a real honour, growing up watching the ARIAs as kids and being on the red carpet with so many other talented musicians, it's awesome,” Took said.
Kevin Parker is just a student
We knew Kevin Parker would win an award tonight, because he’s about to pick up the Global Impact Award.
It's also no great surprise to see him win Best Producer.
Parker has produced all the Tame Impala records (Parker is Tame Impala if you’re catching up) and it’s his openminded approach to making records that has kept him so beloved.
“I still feel like I’m learning”
“I still feel like I’m learning”
He won this same award in 2015 and 2021, and if he keeps reshaping pop music the way he does in the past decade or so, we’ll see him up here again.
Tame Impala wins Producer — Best Produced Release
• Ninajirachi for 2charm — Star Scum City [STAR SCUM RECORDS]
• Ninajirachi / Porter Robinson for Ninajirachi — WannaCry [NLV RECORDS]
DMA'S win Best Group
• 5 Seconds of Summer — Everyone's A Star! [Republic Records]
Who is Ecca Vandal?
If you're only just hearing about Breakthrough Artist winner Ecca Vandal, it's time to catch up.

The South African-born artist has been making great music for years - her self-titled debut album came out in 2017 - but it's this year's Looking For People To Unfollow that has her the talk of the Australian music scene right now.
For good reason too, it's a hell of a record. Here's what Al Newstead wrote about it in May.

Brandishing metal, neo-soul, pop, hip hop, punk, R&B — you name it — Vandal refuses to be boxed in, showcasing her versatility to dizzying effect without forgetting the hooks.She'll growl with a rapper's ferocity over distorted riffs one moment, soar to a candy-coated refrain the next, sounding like Gwen Stefani fronting Violent Soho.
Brandishing metal, neo-soul, pop, hip hop, punk, R&B — you name it — Vandal refuses to be boxed in, showcasing her versatility to dizzying effect without forgetting the hooks.
She'll growl with a rapper's ferocity over distorted riffs one moment, soar to a candy-coated refrain the next, sounding like Gwen Stefani fronting Violent Soho.
She's still up for a few more awards, including the big one for Album of the Year.
Ecca Vandal wins Michael Gudinski Breakthrough Artist
• aleksiah — Good On Paper [Chugg Music & Stellar Trigger / MGM]
• WILSN — Bloom [Mushroom Music]
Country's new star
Who You Are is the debut album from Cherrybook's new favourite daughter Rachel Fahim.
She won Tamworth's popular Star Maker competition in 2017, and she's also up for the Michael Gudiniski Breakthrough Artist Awards right now!
Rachael Fahim wins Best Country Album
• Wade Forster — Gooseneck Party [Community Music]
Boy's got soul
Boy Soda won this award last year too!
The Sydney artist scored five nominations this year and is still in the running for Album of the Year and Best Solo Artist.
He used his speech to shout out fellow nominees Miss Kaninna and Becca Hatch.
R&B to the front. I’m so honoured to be here amongst such amazing names.
BOY SODA wins Best Soul/R&B Release
• Becca Hatch — Garden (Bang Goes the Drum) [G.Y.R.O.]
• BOY SODA — Soulstar [Warner Music Australia]
Genesis Owusu delivers a blistering rendition of his song Stampede
He's up for eight awards at tonight's ARIAs, including Album of the Year, for his new record Redstar Wu & The Worldwide Scourge.
A win would be his third in the category.
When he won in 2023, he called on the audience to “pay attention to what is happening in the world”, proclaiming: “Ceasefire now, ceasefire now, free Palestine.”
Alex the Astronaut brought a briefcase onto the red carpet
Singer-songwriter Alex the Astronaut has brought a touch of business chic to the red carpet, packing a briefcase for tonight’s event.
“I like coming to the ARIAs," they said. "It’s a very long day, so I thought I’d come prepared with my briefcase."
Inside: all the night-out essentials of course — a change of shoes and socks, a drink bottle, mints and a phone charger.
The Sydney-based artist took a firm but comedic stance on the use of AI in Aussie music, which has been a hot topic on the red carpet.
“It’s kind of like boomers and Facebook, like there was so long where people would believe facts then their kids would go, 'Do you realise that’s not true?'" they said.
"I think we’re gonna get really good at telling what’s AI."
Several bodies representing Australia’s creative and media industry have come together tonight to take a stand on AI at tonight's ARIA Awards.
The "Not AI’s to Take" campaign is pushing for AI platforms to get permission and offer payment before using Australian work to train their models.
Emma Donovan is a river girl
Emma Donovan's win is richly deserved.
For decades she's been one of our country's most powerful and beautiful voices, making incredible records across country, soul, blues and more.
Take Me To The River sees her dive into the soul classics that have been a huge inspiration to her. But this isn't your regular covers album. In Donovan's hands, these songs have a whole new power.
In her super emotional speech, she pays tribute to the water that inspired her when making the album.
"I'm known as a river girl. There's a lot of rivers up home under threat. I want to say thank you to the fresh water and salt water, because that really healed me."
If you want to know what all the fuss is about, have a listen to this incredible performance she recently did with the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra.
Emma Donovan wins Best Blues & Roots Album
Alternative is back!
Ecca Vandal is the first winner of Best Alternative Release in a decade as the category was discontinued after Sarah Blasko's win back in 2016.
Regurgitator and You Am I hold the record for most wins in the category. Both of them have two wins apiece.
Ecca spent her speech thanking her team, with a special dedication to the album's producer (and her partner) Richie Buxton.
The ARIAs are shouting out the Hall of Fame's latest inductees
Ecca Vandal wins Best Alternative Release
• Meg Mac — It's My Party [EMI Music Australia]
Ninajirachi and Porter Robinson win Best Dance/Electronic Release
• Dean Turnley — Actin' Tough [CHAOS in collaboration with HOME//GRXWN]
• Dom Dolla — Addicted to Bass [TMRW Music]
• Yes Boone — All I Really Want [TMRW Music]
G Flip invites their drummer to speak
Honestly after watching G Flip's incredible One Night Stand performance from last year, it's tough to argue that they deserve the award for Best Australian Live Act.
They played tons of big shows locally this year in support of their third album Dream Ride and those performances were on a truly epic scale.
"No one is best live act," they said "Everyone in this category is so phenomenal."
They graciously invited drummer Benji on stage who said he's never worked with someone as dedicated as G Flip in his 27 years of performing.
G Flip wins Best Australian Live Act
• Baker Boy — Djandjay Tour [Handsome Tours]
• BOY SODA — Lil Obsession Tour [Select Music]
• G Flip — Dream Ride Tour — Australia 2026
• Gang Of Youths — Various
• Paul Kelly — Australian Tour 2025 [Frontier Touring]
Who are our ARIA hosts?
Or as Bracewell quipped in their opening remarks, she's "two Veronicas stacked on top of each other".
It's a pretty joke- and reference-dense opening salvo, tackling everything from rental bonds to break-out hit Eastern Rosellas and sniffer dogs at music festivals.
It's a super fun way to kick off the 40th anniversary of the ARIAs.
We've also got TV presenter and author Georgie Tunny backstage.
Key Event
Darren Hayes gets us started
Seeing Darren Hayes on the ARIAs stage was a genuine surprise, but a very welcome one.
He performed Savage Garden’s 1999 song Affirmation, one of the last singles they released before breaking up in 2001.
That band is forever part of ARIAs history. Back in 1997, they won no fewer than 10 awards on the night. Hayes has won 14 ARIAs across his career.
If you’re feeling brave – dive into his stunning Take 5. Make sure you have tissues handy.
Key Event
The Wiggles don't feel any rivalry with their fellow nominees
The Wiggles have swapped out their signature brightly-coloured turtlenecks for some red carpet glamour.
The group’s album Sparkle! A Circus Of Lights is nominated for Best Children’s Album, going head to head with some other big hitters in kids TV, like Play School and Bluey.
Simon Wiggle, aka Simon Pryce, remained very diplomatic when asked by ABC News on the red carpet about rivalry in the category.
“We don’t really see it that way — what we do is just about trying to create great music for children,” he said.
“That’s the intention for all of us.”
While he said he’s hoping to catch up with plenty of “old friends and old faces” tonight, he also let us in on his culinary hopes for this evening.
“A little medium rare steak, some bubbly water and some fruit salad I hope,” Pryce said.
Good to know he practices what he preaches!
Key Event
Who's going to win Album of the Year?
It really feels like the top prize of Album of the Year could be anyone's game.
I reckon there are three frontrunners:
• Ecca Vandal, who took out the $50,000 Australian Music Prize just last week, for her second album Looking for People to Unfollow;
• Genesis Owusu, who won Album of the Year for his first two records, in 2021 and 2023, and could make it three for three with his third album, Redstar Wu & the Worldwide Scourge; and

• Tame Impala, aka Perth's Kevin Parker for his fifth album Deadbeat. Parker landed a Grammy nomination this week and also has an impressive ARIA track record, winning Album of the Year for his last three albums, in 2013, 2015 and 2020 (but he missed out for his debut in 2010).
Personally, I'd like to see someone new take it out, like BOY SODA for his debut Soulstar, because his soulful grooves remind me of Frank Ocean.

An outside chance is Sydney-formed rock band DMA'S, for their self-titled fifth album. They've never landed the top prize before, but did win Best Group in 2023, and landed at #1 on ARIA's Top 20 Australian Albums chart at the end of August.
Could 2026 finally be their year?
Time will tell, friends. But my gut is saying this one is going to Tame Impala, who capped off a national arena tour at the end of last month.

They're a chance for local musicians to party acknowledge each other's achievements over the last year.
